## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (three Suggestion-level findings, no checklist failures)
The pull request is ready to merge: all 60 checklist items passed, including the eight acceptance-criteria items, and the reviewers raised only three minor suggestions, none of which blocks the change.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/tools/_format.py` lines 389-404: no test checks `query_info["row_count"]` when the last `run_sql` in a turn is an introspection query whose result is withheld. The only new test that asserts the row count runs the data query last, so a refactor that moved the row-count update into the non-introspection branch would leave `row_count` as `None` for a turn ending on a catalog lookup and no test would fail. The impact is low, because `query_info` reaches clients only when `show_details` is on. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 290-299: when `components_to_blocks` raises, the new handler re-raises the sanitized internal error before `build_agent_trace` runs, so with `show_details` on the client gets no `_meta["sqllens/agent_trace"]` for this failure. The sibling `AgentRunError` path does ship the trace. The failure still surfaces as a structured `isError`, so this is lost context, not a silent failure. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `tests/unit/test_safety.py` lines 855-858: the comment "An inline comment right after SHOW is caught by the parse root." heads three test cases, but the third, `("/* a /* b */ c */ SHOW TABLES", "postgres")`, is a nested leading comment, not an inline comment after `SHOW`. The tests are unaffected; only the label is wrong.
